question.problem: The function ${y}_{1}(x)=x$ is a solution to the equation ${x}^{2}{y}^{″}+5x{y}^{′}-5y=0$ for $x>0.$ If ${y}_{2}=u(x){y}_{1}(x)$ is a second solution of the equation, then which of the following equations must be satisfied by $u(x)?$
question.worked_solution:
We're given that

$$
{y}_{2}(x)=u(x){y}_{1}(x)=ux.
$$

Differentiating ${y}_{2}=ux$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{2}^{′} & ={u}^{′}x+u \\ {y}_{2}^{″} & ={u}^{″}x+2{u}^{′}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}({u}^{″}x+2{u}^{′})+5x({u}^{′}x+u)-5ux & =0 \\ {u}^{″}{x}^{3}+2{u}^{′}{x}^{2}+5{u}^{′}{x}^{2}+5ux-5ux & =0 \\ {u}^{″}{x}^{3}+7{u}^{′}{x}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}({u}^{″}x+7{u}^{′}) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${x}^{2}\ne 0$ for $x>0,$ we must have

$$
x{u}^{″}+7{u}^{′}=0.
$$
